newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kidd elected speaker of NZ parliament.
newsitem.headline: Kidd elected speaker of NZ parliament.

text.p: National MP and former energy minister Doug Kidd was elected speaker of the New Zealand parliament on Thursday.
The vote was 70-50 in favour of Kidd over Labour's Jonathan Hunt. National, Act, New Zealand First and United voted together for Kidd, and Labour and the Alliance against.
Under new standing orders, the speaker has a deliberative vote but not a casting vote.

Under the standing orders which applied in the last parliament, the election of the speaker effectively lowered the vote of his or her party by one because the speaker's vote was only used to break a deadlock and by convention was always used for the status quo.
Under the new arrangement, the speaker has a deliberative vote on every issue, so is free to vote for his party.
National has 44 seats and its coalition partner New Zealand First has 17. Labour has 37, the Alliance 13, Act eight and United one.
New Treasurer Winston Peters sat apart from the bloc of New First MPs, taking his place in the deputy prime minister's seat on the National Party's front bench.
